public_rationale: The reviewed estimates have empirical foundations, documented assumptions and cross-checks. They also contain substantial uncertainty and incomplete coverage. That evidence does not establish that almost all estimates are guesses, but a few documented methods cannot settle the broad claim in the opposite direction.
limitations: The research is not a representative audit of the estimation industry.
Calling all uncertain estimates 'guesses' would make the claim much weaker than its ordinary contextual reading.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Essentially all AI compute capacity estimates are guesses.

statement.excerpt: As a result, basically any AI compute capacity estimates are guesses.

our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion concerns estimates of installed or available AI compute, especially company and industry totals.
The plain reading is that almost all such estimates lack a sufficiently verified empirical foundation. Merely having uncertainty does not make an estimate a guess.
Use the latest completed quarter before publication, July–September 2026, to assess the contemporary estimation methods. Earlier methodological publications are context.
A few well-documented facilities would not by themselves disprove a claim qualified by 'basically'.
criteria.support_condition: A representative examination of contemporary capacity estimates shows that nearly all depend principally on unverified assumptions about operational capacity.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A substantial, representative set of contemporary estimates has documented operational inputs and credible validation sufficient to distinguish it from guesswork.

evidence.excerpt: We defer to the power model since it is more confident and robust: OpenAI directly disclosed its power capacity at the end of 2024 and 2025, while the spending model needs to make more assumptions to convert yearly spending totals to point-in-time run rates.
evidence.locator: OpenAI — Modeling, comparison with the cloud-spending model
evidence.explanation: The method uses disclosed capacity and an alternative model as a cross-check. This challenges the implication of wholly ungrounded guessing, but does not independently verify the disclosures or establish the quality of nearly all estimates.

evidence.excerpt: Power capacity itself is estimated from satellite imagery, public disclosures, and permitting documents. A few sites, like Colossus 1 and 2, disclosed chip types and counts directly, giving more confident estimates.
evidence.explanation: This earlier publication describes real evidential inputs alongside modeling assumptions. It also reports limited global coverage, so it establishes neither comprehensive knowledge nor near-universal guesswork.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A representative review of estimates available before publication, with independent checks of their operational inputs and a stated standard for adequate verification.
